hints: Look at what each test is really searching for, bromine water finds a C=C double bond while Tollens' reagent finds an easily oxidised aldehyde.
Check the three structures for those groups, only $\text{CH}_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ contains $\text{C=C}$ and only $\text{C}_3\text{H}_7\text{CHO}$ contains $\text{-CHO}$.
Match each positive compound to its test column to pick the row that pairs the alkene with bromine water and the aldehyde with Tollens' reagent.
walkthrough:
**Identify the three functional groups**

First, let's be friendly with the three compounds. $\text{C}_3\text{H}_7\text{CHO}$ is an aldehyde, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_3$ is a ketone, and $\text{CH}_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ is an unsaturated alcohol with a C=C bond.

Think of it as: -CHO, C=O in the middle, and C=C plus -OH.

**Who decolourises bromine water?**

Bromine water is decolourised by electrophilic addition across a carbon-carbon double bond. Only the unsaturated alcohol has $\text{C=C}$.

$$\text{CH}_2\text{=CH- + Br}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_2\text{Br-CHBr-}$$

**Who gives a silver mirror with Tollens?**

Tollens' reagent, $\text{[Ag(NH}_3\text{)}_2\text{]}^+$, is a mild oxidising agent. It oxidises aldehydes to carboxylates but cannot oxidise ketones or alcohols under these conditions.

$$\text{RCHO + 2[Ag(NH}_3\text{)}_2\text{]}^+ + 3\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{RCOO}^- + 2\text{Ag + 4NH}_3 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Pick the correct row**

So bromine water is decolourised by $\text{CH}_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ and the silver mirror is formed by $\text{C}_3\text{H}_7\text{CHO}$. That combination matches the correct row.

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{C}_3\text{H}_7\text{CHO}$ is saturated so it cannot add bromine and will not decolourise bromine water. $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_3$ is a ketone and resists oxidation by Tollens' reagent, so no silver mirror forms.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_3$ has no C=C bond so it leaves bromine water orange. The second half is right that $\text{C}_3\text{H}_7\text{CHO}$ gives Tollens' test, but the first half is wrong.
options.C: Incorrect. The first half is right that $\text{CH}_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ decolourises bromine water due to its alkene group. The second half is wrong because $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_3$ is a ketone and is not oxidised by Tollens' reagent.
options.D: Correct. $\text{CH}_2\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ contains $\text{CH}_2\text{=CH-}$ which undergoes addition with $\text{Br}_2$ and decolourises bromine water. $\text{C}_3\text{H}_7\text{CHO}$ is the only aldehyde, so it is the only one oxidised by Tollens' reagent to give the silver mirror of Ag.
